exposure: maternal age (adolescent: 10-19 years vs. adult: >=20 years)
cohort: The study included adolescents aged 10-19 years with singleton pregnancies of at least 28 weeks of gestation, compared to women aged >=20 years meeting the same criteria, delivering at Nianankoro Fomba Hospital.
finding: Compared with adult women, adolescent deliveries were significantly associated with increased maternal, fetal, and perinatal risks.
mod_finding: Adolescents had slightly higher instrumental delivery rates and significantly increased cesarean section rates compared to adult women.
